players.product: Falcon platform AI: Charlotte AI detection triage and SafeMind agentic security, run on rented AI compute (Cerebras inference, CoreWeave GPUs, NVIDIA NIM)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K, fiscal 2026 (year ended January 31, 2026): total revenue $4,812,005 thousand, up 22% (subscription $4,564,683 thousand, up 21%; professional services $247,322 thousand, up 29%); subscription gross margin 78% and total gross margin 75%, both flat; ARR $5,252,751 thousand at January 31, 2026, up 24%; the United States was 67% of revenue; no channel partner or direct customer represented 10% or more of total revenue in fiscal 2026, 2025 or 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenue $4,812,005 thousand, up 22%; ARR $5,252,751 thousand, up 24%

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: backlog of approximately $4.2 billion as of January 31, 2026 (contract amounts not yet invoiceable); remaining performance obligations $9.0 billion, of which approximately 51% is expected to be recognized in the following 12 months and 43% in 13 to 36 months; deferred revenue $4.8 billion, $3.4 billion of it current; purchases of property and equipment $302,108 thousand in fiscal 2026 versus $254,852 thousand in fiscal 2025.

10-K: CrowdStrike relies on a limited number of suppliers for several components of the equipment it uses to operate its cloud platform, buys them on a purchase order basis without long-term contracts guaranteeing supply, and says component shortages and price increases could delay new data centers and capacity increases; in the public sector, 25 of the 50 U.S. states have standardized on CrowdStrike's platform at the enterprise level, Department of Defense organizations can rely on its Impact Level 5 provisional authorization, and customers can deploy Falcon in AWS GovCloud.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 of the 50 U.S. states standardized on the platform
